title: Five Navy Planes Vanished. So Did The Plane Sent To Find Them.
description:
In 1945, five Navy bombers vanished on a routine training flight. The rescue plane sent to find them vanished too. No wreckage from any of them has ever been found.

#shorts #truestory #unsolvedmystery
sources: Smithsonian Magazine's account of the Flight 19 disappearance
Naval History and Heritage Command's official loss report on Flight 19
History.com's coverage of the Bermuda Triangle squadron disappearance

scenes.text: On 05/12/1945, five Navy bomber planes took off from Fort Lauderdale for a routine training flight, and none of them ever came back.

The flight was led by Lieutenant Charles Taylor, a combat veteran with twenty five hundred hours of flying experience. Two hours in, he radioed that his compass had failed and he didn't know his position.
The other four pilots reported the same thing. Their instruments were failing too, and radio contact grew fainter as their fuel ran out.
The Navy sent a rescue plane carrying thirteen more men to find them. It also vanished, dropping off radio contact mid-flight.
In total, six aircraft and twenty seven men disappeared that day. Despite one of the largest air and sea searches in history, no confirmed wreckage from any of them has ever been found.
The official Navy view is that the planes drifted out over open ocean and ran out of fuel. But the case is part of what built the entire legend of the Bermuda Triangle.
